title: Highest Weights and Rational Representations of Split Reductive Groups

items.title: Weights, dominant weights and the highest-weight order of a rational representation
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $(G,T)$ be a split reductive group over $k$ with Weyl
group $W$ and root datum $(X,\Phi,\alpha\mapsto\alpha^\vee)$, $X=X(T)$, and let
$B\supseteq T$ be a Borel subgroup with system of positive roots $\Phi^+$ and
base $\Delta$
([[def-split-reductive-algebraic-group]],
[[def-roots-and-root-groups-of-a-split-reductive-group]],
[[thm-root-subgroups-of-a-split-reductive-group]],
[[lem-character-and-cocharacter-lattices-of-a-split-torus]]). For a rational
representation $(V,r)$ of $G$
([[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]]) the
$T$-weight decomposition is $V=\bigoplus_{\chi\in X}V_\chi$ with
$V_\chi=\{v\in V:\rho(v)=v\otimes e_\chi\}$
([[lem-representations-of-diagonalizable-groups-are-sums-of-eigenspaces]]); the
**weights** of $(V,r)$ are the characters $\chi$ with $V_\chi\ne0$, and
$V_\chi$ is the **weight space** of $\chi$. An element $\lambda\in X$ is
**dominant** if $\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ge0$ for every
$\alpha\in\Phi^+$ (equivalently, for every $\alpha\in\Delta$); write $X^+$ for
the set of dominant weights. Define a partial order on $X$ by $\lambda\ge\mu$ if
and only if
$\lambda-\mu=\sum_{\alpha\in\Delta}m_\alpha\alpha$ with
$m_\alpha\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$. The **fundamental weights** $\omega_i$
($i\in\Delta$) are the unique elements of $\mathbb Q\Phi\subseteq
X\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$ dual to the simple coroots,
$\langle\omega_i,\alpha_j^\vee\rangle=\delta_{ij}$; they form a
basis of $\mathbb Q\Phi$ and every $\lambda\in X\otimes\mathbb Q$
decomposes as
$\lambda=\sum_i\langle\lambda,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle\omega_i+\lambda_0$ with
$\lambda_0$ pairing to $0$ with every coroot
([[lem-root-datum-combinatorics]]).
items.strategy: Definition record following Milne 22.1, 22.3 and 22.8 with the conventions of 21.35: weights are the nontrivial $T$-eigenspaces of the comodule, dominance is tested on $\Phi^+$ or $\Delta$, and the order is generated by the positive simple roots. The weight decomposition is the batch-18 eigenspace theorem applied to the split torus; the fundamental weights use the lattice duality of batch 19. No Choice is used in the definition itself; the cited suppliers carry the assumptions recorded on their own pages.

items.title: Primitive vectors for a Borel pair
items.statement:
Let $(G,T)$ be a split reductive group, $B\supseteq T$ a Borel subgroup with
unipotent radical $U=B_u$ and roots $\Phi$
([[def-borel-subgroup-and-maximal-torus]],
[[def-unipotent-algebraic-group]],
[[def-roots-and-root-groups-of-a-split-reductive-group]],
[[thm-root-subgroups-of-a-split-reductive-group]]). Let $(V,r)$ be a rational
representation
([[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]]). A
nonzero vector $v\in V$ is **primitive** (for the pair $(B,T)$) if it spans a
$B$-stable line. Such a vector is fixed by $U$ and is a $T$-eigenvector: the action on its one-dimensional line restricts to a character of $T$, and unipotence forces the action of $U$ on that line to be trivial. Assuming the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) for the cited split-Borel structure, multiplication is an isomorphism $U\rtimes T\to B$, as justified in the Remarks below. Consequently the converse holds as well: a nonzero $U$-fixed $T$-eigenvector is primitive.
The **weight** of a primitive vector is the character $\lambda\in X(T)$ with
$t\cdot v=\lambda(t)v$ for all $t$ and all $k$-algebras; for a finite-dimensional
$V$ it is the weight $\lambda$ with $v\in V_\lambda$
([[def-weight-and-dominant-weight-of-a-rational-representation]]).

items.title: Expansion of a root-group translate of a weight vector
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $(V,r)$ be a
rational representation of a split reductive group $(G,T)$, let $v\in V_\lambda$
be a weight vector, and let $\alpha\in\Phi$ with root-group isomorphism
$u_\alpha:\mathbf G_a\to U_\alpha$
([[thm-root-subgroups-of-a-split-reductive-group]]). These coordinates satisfy
$t\,u_\alpha(c)\,t^{-1}=u_\alpha(\alpha(t)c)$ over every $k$-algebra.
Then there are vectors
$v_i\in V_{\lambda+i\alpha}$ ($i\ge1$), only finitely many nonzero, such that
$$u_\alpha(c)\cdot v=v+\sum_{i\ge1}c^i v_i$$
for every $c$ (and every $k$-algebra after base change). In particular the orbit
map $c\mapsto u_\alpha(c)\cdot v$ is polynomial with constant term $v$ and
higher coefficients in the stated weight spaces.
items.strategy: Milne 22.14 (Steinberg Lemma 72): write the polynomial expansion $u_\alpha(c)v=\sum_{i\ge0}c^iv_i$ using rationality, then conjugate by $t\in T$ and use $tu_\alpha(c)t^{-1}=u_\alpha(\alpha(t)c)$ to obtain $t\cdot v_i=\lambda(t)\alpha(t)^iv_i$; setting $c=0$ gives $v_0=v$. The root-group isomorphism and the conjugation formula are batch-19 items. The argument is a direct computation and uses no Choice beyond the cited suppliers.

items.title: The normalizer of the torus permutes weight spaces
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $(V,r)$ be a
rational representation of a split reductive group $(G,T)$ and let
$n\in N_G(T)(R)$ for a $k$-algebra $R$. If $v\in V_\lambda$, then $n\cdot(v\otimes1)\in(V\otimes_kR)_{n\lambda}$, where $n\lambda:T_R\to\mathbf G_{m,R}$ is the character $t\mapsto\lambda(n^{-1}tn)$, tested over every $R$-algebra. If $R$ is disconnected, this character can vary between components; the target denotes its eigensubmodule over $R$. Consequently, for every $w\in W(G,T)$ the weight spaces
$V_\lambda$ and $V_{w\lambda}$ have the same dimension, and the set of weights
of $(V,r)$ is stable under $W$
([[thm-weyl-group-borel-chambers]],
[[def-root-datum-of-a-split-reductive-group]]).
items.strategy: Direct proof on the current carrier: 1.1, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1; For $t\in T(R)$ one computes $t\cdot(n\cdot v)=n\cdot((n^{-1}tn)\cdot v)=n\cdot(\lambda(n^{-1}tn)v)=\lambda(n^{-1}tn)\,(n\cdot v)=(n\lambda)(t)\,(n\cdot v)$ in $V_R$: the first equality uses that the action is a left action and $n^{-1}tn\in T(R)$, and the second uses [F2] and $R$-linearity of the action of $n$. Hence $n\cdot(v\otimes1)$ belongs to the stated eigensubmodule of $V\otimes_kR$, with the calculation valid over every $R$-algebra.

items.title: Modules generated by a primitive vector
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $(V,r)$ be a
rational representation of a split reductive group $(G,T)$ (not necessarily
finite-dimensional) that is generated as a $G$-module by a primitive vector $v$
of weight $\lambda$
([[def-primitive-vector-of-a-rational-representation]]). Then: (a) $V$ is
generated as a module over the opposite unipotent group $U^-$ by $v$; (b)
$V=kv\oplus\bigoplus_{\mu<\lambda}V_\mu$, where every weight $\mu$ of $V$ has
the form $\mu=\lambda-\sum_{\alpha\in\Delta}m_\alpha\alpha$ with
$m_\alpha\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, and $V_\lambda=kv$ has dimension one; (c)
$\lambda$ is dominant; (d) the sum of all proper $G$-stable subspaces of $V$ is
proper, so $V$ has a largest proper $G$-submodule and the quotient by it is a
simple $G$-module generated by the image of $v$.

Let $Z$ be the $U^-$-submodule generated by $v$, defined as the span of the coefficients of its $U^-$-coaction. items.title: Simple rational representations have a unique highest weight
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $(V,r)$ be a
simple rational representation of a split reductive group $(G,T)$ with Borel
subgroup $B\supseteq T$ ([[def-borel-subgroup-and-maximal-torus]], [[thm-root-subgroups-of-a-split-reductive-group]]). Then: (a)
$V$ contains a primitive vector $v$, and it is unique up to multiplication by a
nonzero scalar; (b) its weight $\lambda$ is dominant and the weight space
$V_\lambda=kv$ is one-dimensional; (c) every weight $\mu$ of $V$ satisfies
$\mu\le\lambda$, i.e. $\mu=\lambda-\sum_{\alpha\in\Delta}m_\alpha\alpha$ with
$m_\alpha\ge0$; (d) any two primitive vectors of $V$ have the same weight; this
weight is called the **highest weight** of $V$.
items.strategy: Direct proof on the current carrier: 1.1, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1; By [F1] and [F2], and the finite-dimensionality of $V$ from [F3], the $B$-module $V$ has a complete flag of subrepresentations; its last line is a $B$-stable line $kv$ with $v\ne0$, so $v$ is primitive.

items.statement: Let $G$ be an affine group scheme of finite type over a field $k$. Then every simple rational representation $(V,r)$ of $G$ is finite-dimensional ([[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]], [[def-simple-and-semisimple-representations]]).

items.title: Simple modules with equal highest weight are isomorphic
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $V_1,V_2$ be simple rational representations of a split reductive group $(G,T)$ with the same highest weight $\lambda$ ([[thm-simple-rational-representations-have-a-highest-weight]]). Then $V_1\cong V_2$.
items.strategy: Milne 22.19 (Steinberg Theorem 39(e) uniqueness): let $v_i$ be primitive vectors of weight $\lambda$ and let $V\subseteq V_1\oplus V_2$ be the submodule generated by $v_1+v_2$. By [[prop-module-generated-by-a-primitive-vector]] the $\lambda$-weight space of $V$ is the line $k(v_1+v_2)$; projection to $V_2$ is surjective and its kernel $V\cap V_1$ is a proper submodule of the simple module $V_1$, hence zero, so the projection is an isomorphism; symmetrically for $V_1$.

items.title: The induced coordinate module E(lambda)
items.statement:
Let $(G,T)$ be a split reductive group over $k$, and let $B^0=B^-$ be a provided opposite Borel subgroup. For a provided character of $B^0$ whose restriction to $T$ is $\lambda\in X(T)$, define $E(\lambda)$ to be the $k$-subspace of $O(G)$ ([[def-coordinate-hopf-algebra-of-affine-group-scheme]]) satisfying
$$f(gb)=f(g)\lambda(b^{-1})$$
for every $k$-algebra $R$, $g\in G(R)$ and $b\in B^0(R)$. Here $\lambda$ on $B^0$ denotes that provided extension. The subspace is stable under the **left** regular action $(gf)(x)=f(g^{-1}x)$ and hence is a rational $G$-module ([[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]]). Its underlying subspace and this action are choice-free. In the source convention this is $\operatorname{Ind}_{B^0}^G(k_\lambda)$.

Assuming AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) for the cited split-Borel structure, $B^0=U^-\rtimes T$ by the dimension-and-exact-image argument in the Remarks of [[def-primitive-vector-of-a-rational-representation]], applied to the opposite Borel. The projection to $T$ extends every $\lambda\in X(T)$ uniquely to a character of $B^0$ trivial on $U^-$. Thus the construction applies to every weight $\lambda$ of the given split torus. The same structural input gives $B^-\cap B=T$ and the open big cells $U^-B$ and $UB^0$ ([[thm-root-subgroups-of-a-split-reductive-group]], [[thm-bruhat-decomposition-for-split-reductive-group]], [[def-borel-subgroup-and-maximal-torus]]).

items.title: Primitive vectors of the induced coordinate module
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $E(\lambda)$
be the induced coordinate module of a split reductive group $(G,T)$ with Borel
$B$ and unipotent radical $U=B_u$
([[def-induced-coordinate-module-e-lambda]]). If $E(\lambda)\ne0$, then the
space $E(\lambda)^U$ of $U$-fixed elements is one-dimensional, its nonzero
elements are primitive vectors of weight $\lambda$
([[def-primitive-vector-of-a-rational-representation]]), and evaluation at the
identity $f\mapsto f(1)$ is an isomorphism $E(\lambda)^U\to k$. In particular
$E(\lambda)\ne0$ if and only if $E(\lambda)$ contains a primitive vector of
weight $\lambda$, unique up to scalar.
items.strategy: Direct proof on the current carrier: 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1; If $f\in E(\lambda)$ vanishes on $U$, then $f=0$: by [F5] $f$ vanishes on the whole big cell $U\cdot B^0$ [F1], and [F2] applies.

items.title: Simple and semisimple rational representations
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be an affine group scheme of finite type over $k$, and let $(V,r)$ be a rational representation of $G$, with subrepresentations the subcomodules of $V$ ([[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]]). The representation $(V,r)$ is **simple** (or **irreducible**) if $V\ne0$ and the only subrepresentations of $V$ are $0$ and $V$. It is **semisimple** (or **completely reducible**) if $V$ is an internal direct sum of simple subrepresentations, $$V=\bigoplus_{i\in I}S_i,\qquad S_i\subseteq V\text{ simple};$$ the zero representation is semisimple, being the empty direct sum.
items.strategy: Definition record following Milne 4.15-4.17, with the direct-sum formulation of semisimplicity and the terminology simple/irreducible, semisimple/completely reducible; subrepresentations are subcomodules by the correspondence of the cited definition. No Choice is used.

items.title: Tensor products, exterior powers and Hom spaces of finite-dimensional rational representations are rational
items.statement: Let $G$ be an affine group scheme of finite type over a field $k$ with coordinate Hopf algebra $A=O(G)$, and let $(V,r)$ and $(W,s)$ be finite-dimensional rational representations with comodule maps $\rho_V:V\to V\otimes_kA$, $\rho_W:W\to W\otimes_kA$ ([[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]]). (a) The formula $c(v\otimes w)=\sum_{i,j}v_i\otimes w_j\otimes a_ib_j$ for $\rho_V(v)=\sum_iv_i\otimes a_i$ and $\rho_W(w)=\sum_jw_j\otimes b_j$ defines the unique comodule structure on $V\otimes_kW$ whose associated rational representation is $g\cdot(v\otimes w)=g\cdot v\otimes g\cdot w$. (b) The space $\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,W)$ carries a rational representation with $(g\cdot f)(v)=g\cdot f(g^{-1}\cdot v)$, and the canonical $k$-linear map $V^*\otimes_kW\to\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,W)$, $\xi\otimes w\mapsto(v\mapsto\xi(v)w)$, where $V^*$ is the contragredient ([[def-contragredient-rational-representation]], [[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]), is an isomorphism of rational representations. (c) For every $d\ge0$ the exterior power $\Lambda^dV$ carries a rational representation with $g\cdot(v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_d)=g\cdot v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge g\cdot v_d$, and for every $k$-algebra $R$ the induced map on $\Lambda^d_R(V_R)$ is $\Lambda^d_R(r_R(g))$ under the identification of the two $R$-modules by the common wedge basis ([[def-kth-exterior-power-by-quotient]], [[thm-increasing-basis-wedges-form-a-basis]]).
items.strategy: Local prerequisite for the codimension-one reduction of complete reducibility (Milne 22.40): the Hom space $\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,W)$ with $(g\cdot f)(v)=g\cdot f(g^{-1}v)$ is a finite-dimensional rational representation, identified with $V^*\otimes W$. The tensor-product comodule structure is verified against the comodule axioms, and the contragredient supplies $V^*$; the canonical map is an isomorphism by the dual basis. This item is a post-scaffold local addition created and authored by the Step 3b auditor; it is registered on the A page before its consumer.

items.title: Power extension over a normal affine domain
items.statement: Let $X$ be an integral affine scheme over a field $k$ whose coordinate ring $A=O(X)$ is a normal domain, i.e. integrally closed in its fraction field ([[def-affine-scheme]], [[thm-global-sections-affine-scheme]], [[def-integral-closure-and-integrally-closed-domain]]). Let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense open subscheme and let $f\in O(U)$ be such that $f^d\in O(X)$ for some integer $d\ge1$, where the rings are compared inside $O(X)\subseteq O(U)\subseteq\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. Then $f\in O(X)$.
items.strategy: Milne 22.23. The element $f$ satisfies the monic polynomial $T^d-f^d\in A[T]$, hence is integral over $A$; since $A$ is a normal domain and $f\in\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, integrality forces $f\in A=O(X)$ ([[def-integral-closure-and-integrally-closed-domain]]). The identification of global sections on the affine scheme is the published affine-sections theorem. The argument is choice-free.

items.title: The top exterior power detects stabilizers of a subspace
items.statement:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over a field $k$, let $W\subseteq V$
be a subspace of dimension $d$, and put $D=\Lambda^dW\subseteq\Lambda^dV$
([[def-kth-exterior-power-by-quotient]], [[def-kth-exterior-power-of-a-linear-map]],
[[cor-dimension-of-the-kth-exterior-power]]). Then for every $k$-algebra $R$ and
every $\alpha\in\operatorname{GL}(V_R)$ one has $\alpha W_R=W_R$ if and only if
$(\Lambda^d\alpha)(D_R)=D_R$. In particular, if $(V,r)$ is a rational
representation of an affine group scheme $G$ over $k$ and $G$ acts on
$\Lambda^dV$ by the exterior power
([[cor-the-top-exterior-power-acts-by-the-determinant]]), then the
scheme-theoretic stabilizer of $W$ in $G$ equals the scheme-theoretic stabilizer
of the line $D$.
items.strategy: Milne 4.28, re-proved locally with the repository's exterior-power convention (no division by $d!$): choose a basis $e_1,\dots,e_d$ of $W$ and $w=e_1\wedge\dots\wedge e_d$; the identity $W_R=\{v\in V_R : w\wedge v=0\}$ holds over every $k$-algebra, so $\alpha$-stability of $W_R$ is equivalent to $\alpha$-stability of the line $kw=D$. Functoriality of $\Lambda^d$ and the top-power determinant identity are the cited published items.

items.title: Chevalley: every closed subgroup is a line stabilizer
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $G$ be an affine group scheme of finite type over a field $k$ and let $H\subseteq G$ be a closed subgroup scheme. Then there exist a finite-dimensional rational representation $(V,r)$ of $G$ and a line $L\subseteq V$ such that $H=\operatorname{Stab}_G(L)$ scheme-theoretically: for every $k$-algebra $R$, $\operatorname{Stab}_G(L)(R)=\{g\in G(R):gL_R=L_R\}$ ([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]], [[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]]). Moreover, if $L=kv$ then $\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\{x\in\operatorname{Lie}(G):xv\in kv\}$.
items.strategy: Milne 4.27-4.29 (Chevalley; Steinberg Lemma 75 gives the independent treatment). Let $\mathfrak a=\ker(O(G)\to O(H))$, a Hopf ideal ([[thm-closed-subgroup-schemes-correspond-to-hopf-ideals]], [[lem-hopf-ideal-kernels-and-quotients]]). Choose a finite-dimensional subcomodule $V\subseteq O(G)$ containing a finite generating set of the ideal $\mathfrak a$ ([[lem-finite-dimensional-subcomodules-contain-elements]]; $O(G)$ is Noetherian). With $W=\mathfrak a\cap V$ one shows that $H$ is the scheme-theoretic stabilizer $G_W$ of the subspace $W$; applying [[lem-top-exterior-power-detects-subspace-stabilizers]] to $\Lambda^{\dim W}V$ replaces $W$ by a line with the same stabilizer. The Lie-algebra equality is Milne 10.31-10.32: applied to the line $L$ it is part (a) of [[lem-lie-algebra-of-the-stabilizer-of-a-subspace-and-lie-stable-subspaces]].

items.title: Primitive vectors from standard maximal parabolics
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $(G,T)$ be a
split reductive group over $k$ with Borel $B\supseteq T$, base
$\Delta=\{\alpha_i\}_{i\in I}$ and fundamental weights $\omega_i$
([[def-weight-and-dominant-weight-of-a-rational-representation]],
[[def-root-datum-of-a-split-reductive-group]]). For every $i\in I$ there exist
a finite-dimensional rational representation $V_i$ of $G$ and a primitive vector
$v_i\in V_i$ whose weight $\lambda_i$ satisfies
$$\langle\lambda_i,\alpha_j^\vee\rangle=0\ (j\ne i),\qquad \langle\lambda_i,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle>0.$$
When the root datum is semisimple,
$\lambda_i=\langle\lambda_i,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle\omega_i$.
items.strategy: Direct proof on the current carrier: 1.1, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 4.1; Let $(V,L)$ be as in [F2] and let $v\ne0$ generate $L$. Since $P_i\supseteq B\supseteq U$ and $P_i\supseteq T$, the line $L$ is $B$-stable, so $v$ is primitive; let $\lambda_i$ be its weight. Replacing $V$ by the $G$-submodule generated by $v$ does not change the line $L$, and by [F3] the weight $\lambda_i$ is then dominant.

items.title: Tensor products of primitive vectors
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $(V,r)$ and $(V',r')$ be rational representations of a split reductive group $(G,T)$ with primitive vectors $v,v'$ of weights $\lambda,\lambda'$ ([[def-primitive-vector-of-a-rational-representation]]). Then $v\otimes v'$ is a primitive vector of $V\otimes V'$ of weight $\lambda+\lambda'$. Consequently tensor powers and tensor products of primitive vectors are primitive, with the summed weights.
items.strategy: Milne 22.25 (Steinberg Theorem 39 and Lemma 76 preamble): $v\otimes v'$ is nonzero (tensor product of nonzero vectors), fixed by the unipotent radical $U$ because each factor is, and is a $T$-eigenvector with character $\lambda+\lambda'$. This is the tensor operation on comodules of batch 13.

items.title: Contragredient (dual) rational representation
items.statement:
Let $(V,r)$ be a finite-dimensional rational representation of an affine group scheme $G$ over $k$
([[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]]). The
**contragredient** representation $r^\vee$ is the representation on the algebraic
dual $V^*=\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)$
([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]) defined by
$$(r^\vee(g)f)(v)=f(r(g)^{-1}v)$$
for $g\in G(R)$, $f\in V^*_R$ and $v\in V_R$. When $V$ is finite-dimensional,
$r^\vee$ is a rational representation and its comodule is the dual comodule of
$(V,r)$; moreover the weights of $(V^*,r^\vee)$ are the negatives of the weights
of $(V,r)$.
items.strategy: Definition record following Milne 22c (the contragredient representation) and Milne 22.26(b); the inverse makes the action a left action, and rationality is checked on the dual comodule. No Choice is used beyond the cited definition of the algebraic dual.

items.title: Central characters and descent along a central isogeny
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $(G,T)$ be a
split semisimple group over $k$ with root system $\Phi$ and root lattice
$Q=\mathbb Z\Phi$ ([[def-root-datum-of-a-split-reductive-group]]). Then: (a)
the scheme-theoretic centre $Z(G)$ equals
$\bigcap_{\alpha\in\Phi}\ker\alpha$, and restriction of characters identifies
$X(Z(G))$ with $X(T)/Q$
([[lem-reductive-center-radical-and-semisimple-quotient]],
[[lem-diagonalizable-character-antiequivalence]]); (b) if $V$ is a simple
rational representation of $G$ of highest weight $\lambda$, then $Z(G)$ acts on
$V$ through the character $\lambda+Q\in X(Z(G))$
([[thm-simple-rational-representations-have-a-highest-weight]]). Now let
$\pi:(G',T')\to(G,T)$ be a central isogeny of split reductive groups, so that
$X(T)\subseteq X(T')$ is a subgroup of finite index. Let $\lambda\in X(T')$ and
let $V'$ be a simple $G'$-module of highest weight $\lambda$; then $V'$ factors
through $G$ if and only if $\lambda\in X(T)$, and the descended $G$-module is
simple. For identification of highest weights, choose Borel subgroups
$B'\supseteq T'$ and $B\supseteq T$ with $\pi(B')=B$; relative to these
compatible source and target Borel pairs, the descended module has highest
weight $\lambda$. Equivalently, for the finite central
subgroup scheme $N=\ker\pi$
([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]]), a simple $G'$-module whose
highest weight lies in $X(T)$ has $N$ acting trivially and hence descends along
the fppf quotient $G'/N=G$
([[thm-fppf-quotient-for-affine-finite-locally-free-equivalence-relation]]).
items.strategy: Direct proof on the current carrier: 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1, 5.1; For (a), first inclusion: let $R$ be a $k$-algebra and let $z\in Z(G)(R)$. By [F1] $z\in T(R)$. Since $z$ is central, $z\,u_\alpha(c)\,z^{-1}=u_\alpha(c)$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi$ and every $c\in R$, while the conjugation formula of [F2] gives $z\,u_\alpha(c)\,z^{-1}=u_\alpha(\alpha(z)c)$. As $u_\alpha$ is an isomorphism of group schemes, $u_\alpha(R)$ is injective, so $\alpha(z)c=c$ for all $c$; setting $c=1$ gives $\alpha(z)=1$. Hence $z\in(\bigcap_{\alpha\in\Phi}\ker\alpha)(R)$ and $Z(G)\subseteq\bigcap_{\alpha\in\Phi}\ker\alpha$.

items.title: Dominant characters of a torus times a split semisimple group are primitive weights
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $Z$ be a
split torus over $k$ and let $G_0$ be a split semisimple group over $k$; put
$G=Z\times G_0$ with the product Borel pair. Let
$\lambda=\lambda_Z+\lambda_0\in X(Z)\oplus X(T_0)$ be dominant for the product
([[def-group-of-multiplicative-type-and-torus]],
[[def-split-reductive-algebraic-group]]). Then there is a rational
representation of $G$ containing a primitive vector of weight $\lambda$; if
$\lambda_0$ is dominant this is obtained by tensoring the one-dimensional
representation of $Z$ of weight $\lambda_Z$ with a representation of $G_0$
carrying a primitive vector of weight $\lambda_0$
([[lem-dominant-characters-of-split-semisimple-groups-arise-as-primitive-weights]],
[[lem-tensor-products-of-primitive-vectors]]).
items.strategy: Direct proof on the current carrier: 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 3.1; In the product $G=Z\times G_0$, regard the one-dimensional representation $k_{\lambda_Z}$ as a $G$-module on which $Z$ acts through $\lambda_Z$ and the factor $G_0$ acts trivially. Its nonzero vectors are fixed by $U=1\times U_0$ and are $T$-eigenvectors of weight $(\lambda_Z,0)$, so each nonzero vector of $k_{\lambda_Z}$ is primitive of weight $(\lambda_Z,0)$ for the pair $(B,T)$.

items.title: Dominant weights classify the simple rational representations of a split reductive group
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $(G,T)$ be a split reductive group over a field $k$, let $B\supseteq T$ be a Borel subgroup, and let $X(T)^+$ be the set of dominant characters of the maximal torus $T$ ([[def-weight-and-dominant-weight-of-a-rational-representation]]). For every $\lambda\in X(T)^+$ there exists a simple rational representation $V(\lambda)$ of $G$, unique up to isomorphism, whose $T$-weight decomposition is $$V(\lambda)=V(\lambda)_\lambda\oplus\bigoplus_{\mu<\lambda}V(\lambda)_\mu$$ with $\dim_kV(\lambda)_\lambda=1$, and every simple rational representation of $G$ is isomorphic to $V(\lambda)$ for a unique $\lambda\in X(T)^+$ ([[thm-simple-rational-representations-have-a-highest-weight]], [[thm-simple-modules-with-equal-highest-weight-are-isomorphic]], [[lem-dominant-characters-arise-as-primitive-weights-for-split-reductive-groups]]). The map sending a simple representation to its highest weight is a bijection from the set of isomorphism classes of simple rational representations of $G$ to $X(T)^+$; it holds in every characteristic.
items.strategy: Milne 22.2 with 22.18-22.20 (the proof route isolated by the design: existence from 22.20, ascent from the semisimple factor and central isogeny, uniqueness from 22.18-22.19). Existence: [[lem-dominant-characters-arise-as-primitive-weights-for-split-reductive-groups]] gives a representation containing a primitive vector of weight $\lambda$; [[prop-module-generated-by-a-primitive-vector]] gives the quotient by the largest proper submodule, a simple module with highest weight $\lambda$, finite-dimensional by [[lem-simple-rational-representations-are-finite-dimensional]]. Uniqueness and the weight description are [[thm-simple-modules-with-equal-highest-weight-are-isomorphic]] and [[thm-simple-rational-representations-have-a-highest-weight]]. No hypothesis on the characteristic is used.

items.title: Lie algebras of subspace stabilizers and Lie-stable subspaces
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $G$ be an
affine group scheme of finite type over a field $k$ with Lie algebra
$\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$
([[def-lie-algebra-of-a-group-scheme]]), let $(V,r)$ be a rational
representation ([[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]]),
and let $W\subseteq V$ be a subspace with scheme-theoretic stabilizer
$\operatorname{Stab}_G(W)$
([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). Then:
(a) $\operatorname{Lie}(\operatorname{Stab}_G(W))=\{x\in\mathfrak g:xW\subseteq W\}$
(Milne 10.31); (b) if moreover $k$ has characteristic $0$, $G$ is connected and
smooth, and $\mathfrak gW\subseteq W$, then $W$ is $G$-stable. In particular a
subspace of a finite-dimensional representation of a connected semisimple group
in characteristic zero is $G$-stable if and only if it is stable under
$\mathfrak g$.
items.strategy: Milne 10.30-10.31 (Steinberg does not need this step). Part (a) reduces to $G=\mathrm{GL}_V$ and computes the tangent space with dual numbers: $\operatorname{id}+\varepsilon\alpha$ stabilizes $W[\varepsilon]$ if and only if $\alpha W\subseteq W$ ([[lem-lie-algebra-of-the-general-linear-group]], [[lem-lie-algebra-tangent-space-and-functoriality]]). For (b), if $\mathfrak gW\subseteq W$ then $\operatorname{Lie}(\operatorname{Stab}_G(W))=\mathfrak g$; Cartier's theorem makes the stabilizer smooth in characteristic zero ([[thm-cartier-smoothness-for-affine-groups-in-characteristic-zero]]) and [[lem-lie-functor-exactness-fixed-points-and-generation]](b) gives $\operatorname{Stab}_G(W)=G$ because $G$ is connected.

items.title: Lie ideals and normal connected subgroups in characteristic zero
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine algebraic group over a field $k$ of characteristic $0$, let $H\subseteq G$ be a smooth closed subgroup scheme with identity component $H^\circ$, and let $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{Lie}(H)\subseteq\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ ([[lem-adjoint-representation-of-an-affine-group-scheme]], [[thm-lie-bracket-and-adjoint-action-from-infinitesimals]]). Then: (a) $[\mathfrak g,\mathfrak h]\subseteq\mathfrak h$ if and only if $H^\circ$ is normal in $G$; (b) if $H$ is normal in $G$, then $[\mathfrak g,\mathfrak h]\subseteq\mathfrak h$. In particular, if $H$ is connected, then $H$ is normal in $G$ if and only if $\mathfrak h$ is an ideal of $\mathfrak g$.
items.strategy: If $[\mathfrak g,\mathfrak h]\subseteq\mathfrak h$, then $\mathfrak h$ is stable under the adjoint action of $\mathfrak g$; [[lem-lie-algebra-of-the-stabilizer-of-a-subspace-and-lie-stable-subspaces]](b) applied to the adjoint representation makes $\mathfrak h$ stable under $G$, and then $gHg^{-1}=H$ for all $g$ by [[lem-lie-functor-exactness-fixed-points-and-generation]](b) (equality of smooth connected subgroups with equal Lie algebras). The converse is immediate from functoriality of Lie and the adjoint action. Cartier's theorem supplies smoothness in characteristic zero.

items.title: The Lie algebra of a semisimple group in characteristic zero is semisimple

items.strategy: Direct proof on the current carrier: 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1, 5.1, 6.1; If a nonzero solvable ideal $\mathfrak r$ exists, take its last nonzero derived term. Jacobi gives $[\mathfrak g,[I,I]]\subseteq[I,I]$ for each ambient ideal $I$, so this term is an ambient ideal, and its next derived term being zero makes it commutative. Thus it suffices to exclude nonzero commutative ideals.

items.title: Trace forms of faithful representations of semisimple Lie algebras are nondegenerate
items.statement:
Let $\mathfrak h$ be a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra over a field
$k$ of characteristic $0$ and let $\rho:\mathfrak h\to\mathfrak{gl}(V)$ be a
faithful finite-dimensional representation with trace form
$B_\rho(x,y)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(x)\rho(y))$
([[def-trace-form-of-a-finite-dimensional-representation]]). Then $B_\rho$ is a
nondegenerate symmetric invariant form on $\mathfrak h$; equivalently, its
radical is zero ([[prop-trace-forms-are-symmetric-and-invariant]]).
items.strategy: The trace form is symmetric and invariant ([[prop-trace-forms-are-symmetric-and-invariant]]), so its radical is an ideal ([[lem-orthogonal-complements-under-invariant-forms-are-ideals]]). If $\mathfrak r$ is that radical, then $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(x)\rho(y))=0$ for all $x\in[\mathfrak r,\mathfrak r]$ and $y\in\mathfrak h$; Cartan's solvability criterion ([[thm-cartans-solvability-criterion]]) makes $\mathfrak r$ solvable. Since $\mathfrak h$ is semisimple, its only solvable ideal is $0$ ([[prop-ideals-and-quotients-of-semisimple-lie-algebras]], [[def-lie-subalgebra-ideal-and-center]]), hence $\mathfrak r=0$ and $B_\rho$ is nondegenerate.

items.title: The Casimir element of a rational representation is an endomorphism of G-modules
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $G$ be a
semisimple algebraic group over a field $k$ of characteristic $0$ and let
$(V,r)$ be a finite-dimensional rational representation with
$\rho:\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak{gl}(V)$ the derived representation and
$\bar{\mathfrak g}=\rho(\mathfrak g)$. If $\bar{\mathfrak g}\ne0$, then:
(a) $\bar{\mathfrak g}$ is a semisimple Lie algebra and the trace form
$B_\rho$ of the faithful representation of $\bar{\mathfrak g}$ on $V$ is
nondegenerate; (b) the Casimir element
$\Omega_{B_\rho}\in U(\bar{\mathfrak g})$ of $B_\rho$ defines a $G$-module endomorphism
$c_V:V\to V$
([[def-casimir-operator-relative-to-an-invariant-form]],
[[lem-the-casimir-operator-is-basis-independent-and-intertwining]]);
(c) $\operatorname{tr}(c_V|_V)=\dim_k\bar{\mathfrak g}$.
Here $U(\bar{\mathfrak g})$ is the universal enveloping algebra, and
$c_V$ is the action of $\Omega_{B_\rho}$ on $V$ induced by the inclusion
$\bar{\mathfrak g}\hookrightarrow\mathfrak{gl}(V)$.
items.strategy: Milne 22c, printed p. 477. By [[lem-lie-algebra-of-a-semisimple-group-in-characteristic-zero-is-semisimple]] $\mathfrak g$ is semisimple, so its quotient $\bar{\mathfrak g}$ is semisimple ([[prop-ideals-and-quotients-of-semisimple-lie-algebras]]) and the trace form of the faithful representation is nondegenerate ([[lem-trace-form-of-a-faithful-representation-of-a-semisimple-lie-algebra-is-nondegenerate]]). The Casimir element $\Omega_{B_\rho}$ is independent of dual bases and central in $U(\bar{\mathfrak g})$, so its operator $c_V$ commutes with $\rho(\mathfrak g)$ ([[lem-the-casimir-operator-is-basis-independent-and-intertwining]]). The line $\langle c_V\rangle\subseteq\operatorname{End}(V)$ is therefore $\mathfrak g$-stable; [[lem-lie-algebra-of-the-stabilizer-of-a-subspace-and-lie-stable-subspaces]](b) makes it $G$-stable, and $X(G)=0$ ([[lem-semisimple-groups-are-perfect-and-have-no-nontrivial-characters]]) forces $G$ to act on it by the trivial character, so $c_V$ is a $G$-endomorphism. The trace identity is the dual-basis computation $\sum_iB_\rho(x_i,x^i)=\dim\bar{\mathfrak g}$.

items.title: Complete reducibility reduces to splitting codimension-one simple submodules
items.statement:
Let $G$ be an algebraic group over a field $k$ with
$X(G)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(G,\mathbf G_m)=0$, so that every one-dimensional
rational representation of $G$ is trivial
([[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]],
[[def-simple-and-semisimple-representations]]). For a possibly nonaffine $G$, a finite-dimensional rational representation here means a morphism $G\to\operatorname{GL}_V$, with subrepresentations the invariant subspaces; this agrees with the cited comodule definition when $G$ is affine. Then the following conditions
are equivalent: (a) every finite-dimensional rational representation of $G$ is
semisimple; (b) every subrepresentation $W$ of codimension one in a
finite-dimensional representation $V$ is a direct summand; (c) every simple
subrepresentation $W$ of codimension one in a finite-dimensional representation
$V$ is a direct summand.
items.strategy: Milne 22.40. The implications (a)$\Rightarrow$(b)$\Rightarrow$(c) are formal. For (c)$\Rightarrow$(b), induct on $\dim V$: if $W$ is not simple choose a nonzero proper submodule $W'$; the quotient $W/W'$ has a complement $V'/W'$ in $V/W'$ by induction, and then $V'/W'$ is one-dimensional and splits by a second induction application. For (b)$\Rightarrow$(a), give $\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,W)$ the $G$-action $(gf)(v)=g\cdot f(g^{-1}v)$; the subspaces of maps restricting to a scalar on $W$ and vanishing on $W$ form a codimension-one pair, and (b) produces a line $L=kf$; since $X(G)=0$, $G$ acts trivially on $L$, so $f$ is $G$-equivariant, and after rescaling $f|_W=\operatorname{id}$; $\ker f$ is the required complement. Iterating gives the direct-sum decomposition.

items.title: Semisimplicity of rational representations descends along field extensions
items.statement:
Let $G$ be an algebraic group over a field $k$, let $(V,r)$ be a
finite-dimensional rational representation and let $k'\supseteq k$ be a field
extension. If the base change $(V_{k'},r_{k'})$ is semisimple as a
representation of $G_{k'}$, then $(V,r)$ is semisimple
([[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]],
[[def-simple-and-semisimple-representations]]). In particular it suffices to
test semisimplicity after extending scalars to an algebraic closure of $k$. For a possibly nonaffine $G$, rationality here means that $r:G\to\operatorname{GL}_V$ is a morphism; subrepresentations are the invariant subspaces. This agrees with the cited comodule definition for affine $G$.
items.strategy: Milne 22.39, from Milne 4.19. For a $G$-submodule $W\subseteq V$, a $G_{k'}$-complement of $W_{k'}$ is a solution of a finite system of $k$-linear equations (the map is $G$-equivariant and restricts to the identity on $W$); a $k$-linear system has a solution over $k$ exactly when its row-reduced echelon form over $k$ admits one, and consistency is preserved by base change ([[thm-gauss-jordan-elimination-produces-reduced-row-echelon-form]]). Hence the complement descends to $k$, and $W$ is a direct summand of $V$. Applying this to every submodule gives semisimplicity.

items.title: Semisimple groups in characteristic zero are linearly reductive
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $G$ be a
semisimple algebraic group over a field $k$ of characteristic $0$. Then every
finite-dimensional rational representation of $G$ is semisimple; equivalently,
$G$ is linearly reductive
([[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]],
[[def-simple-and-semisimple-representations]]).
items.strategy: Milne 22.41 (Steinberg sketches the independent compact-form argument on p. 225). By [[lem-semisimplicity-of-rational-representations-descends-along-field-extensions]] we may assume $k$ algebraically closed; $X(G)=0$ by [[lem-semisimple-groups-are-perfect-and-have-no-nontrivial-characters]], so [[lem-complete-reducibility-reduces-to-codimension-one-simple-submodules]] reduces to splitting a simple submodule $W$ of codimension one in a finite-dimensional $V$. If $V$ is the trivial representation it is semisimple; otherwise let $c_V$ be the Casimir endomorphism of [[lem-casimir-element-of-a-rational-representation-is-an-endomorphism-of-g-modules]]. Since $G$ acts trivially on the one-dimensional quotient $V/W$, $\mathfrak gV\subseteq W$ and hence $c_V(V)\subseteq W$; on the simple module $W$ the endomorphism $c_V$ acts by a scalar $a$ because it is a $\mathfrak g$-intertwiner and $k$ is algebraically closed ([[cor-schurs-lemma-for-irreducible-lie-algebra-representations]]); the trace identity gives $a\dim W=\operatorname{tr}(c_V)=\dim\bar{\mathfrak g}\ne0$, so $a\ne0$. Therefore $\ker c_V$ is a one-dimensional $G$-submodule complementary to $W$ (it is $G$-stable by the Casimir lemma), and [[lem-complete-reducibility-reduces-to-codimension-one-simple-submodules]] completes the proof.

items.title: Complete reducibility of rational modules in characteristic zero
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $G$ be a
connected reductive algebraic group over a field $k$ of characteristic $0$ (in
particular, let $G$ be any split reductive group over such a field). Then the
following are equivalent: (a) $G$ is reductive; (b) every finite-dimensional
rational representation of $G$ is semisimple; (c) some faithful
finite-dimensional rational representation of $G$ is semisimple
([[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]],
[[def-radical-and-unipotent-radical-of-an-algebraic-group]],
[[def-simple-and-semisimple-representations]]). In particular $G$ is linearly
reductive, so every rational representation is a direct sum of simple
representations.
items.strategy: Direct proof on the current carrier: 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 2.1, 3.1; *(b)$\Rightarrow$(c).* By [F4] there is a faithful finite-dimensional rational representation of $G$; if (b) holds, that representation is semisimple, so (c) holds.

items.title: The highest-weight classification does not imply semisimplicity in positive characteristic
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
The classification of
[[thm-dominant-weights-classify-simple-rational-modules-for-split-reductive-groups]]
holds for a split reductive group over every field, but it does not imply that
every rational representation is semisimple. Complete reducibility is a
characteristic-zero phenomenon
([[thm-complete-reducibility-of-rational-modules-in-characteristic-zero]]); in
characteristic $p>0$ a split reductive group need not be linearly reductive, as
the companion counterexample
[[cex-rational-modules-need-not-be-semisimple-in-characteristic-p]] on this
pair's examples page shows (Milne Example 12.55 and Exercise 12-9; Steinberg
Ch. 12, the paragraph after Theorem 39(e)). Readers should not infer
semisimplicity of $\operatorname{Rep}(G)$ from the existence and uniqueness of
simple modules with prescribed dominant highest weight.

The two statements concern different properties: the classification theorem only
asserts that simple modules are parametrized by dominant weights and that the
top weight space is one-dimensional, while semisimplicity of every
finite-dimensional rational representation is a strictly stronger property that
fails already for $\mathrm{SL}_2$ in characteristic $p>0$
([[def-split-reductive-algebraic-group]]).
items.strategy: Remark recording the boundary isolated by the design: the classification theorem A22 is characteristic-free, while the complete-reducibility theorem A32 is restricted to characteristic zero. The positive-characteristic failure is delegated to the B-page counterexample; the sources are Milne 12.55/12.56 and Exercise 12-9 and Steinberg Ch. 12 (representations constructed from a lattice can lose irreducibility in characteristic p). No additional proof obligation is created by the remark.

items.title: The simple modules of SL_2 and its fundamental representation
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $k$ be a
field and $G=\mathrm{SL}_2$ with its diagonal maximal torus $T_2$, upper
triangular Borel $B$ and root datum $X(T_2)=\mathbb Z\chi$, $\alpha=2\chi$,
$\alpha^\vee=\chi^\vee$ ([[def-root-datum-of-a-split-reductive-group]],
[[lem-sl2-structure-and-root-coordinates]]). The fundamental weight is
$\omega=\chi$, the dominant characters are
$X(T_2)^+=\{m\omega:m\ge0\}$, and
[[thm-dominant-weights-classify-simple-rational-modules-for-split-reductive-groups]]
attaches to each $m\ge0$ exactly one simple module $L(m)$, with $L(0)$ the
trivial representation and $L(1)=k^2$ the standard representation
([[def-weight-and-dominant-weight-of-a-rational-representation]]). For every
$m$, $L(m)_{m\chi}$ is one-dimensional and all other weights of $L(m)$ belong
to $\{m\chi,(m-2)\chi,\dots,-m\chi\}$, each with multiplicity at most one; in
particular $\dim_kL(m)\le m+1$. If $p=\operatorname{char}(k)>0$, the vectors
$e_1^p,e_2^p$ span a two-dimensional simple submodule of the symmetric power
$S^p(k^2)$ with highest weight $p\chi$, so this submodule is isomorphic to
$L(p)$, realized as the Frobenius twist of the standard module $L(1)$ through
$g\cdot e_i^p=(g\cdot e_i)^p$.
items.strategy: Apply the classification theorem to the rank-one root datum of batch 19 (Milne 22.33), using only A-page suppliers of batch 19; the dominant characters and the simple standard module are computed directly. [[thm-simple-rational-representations-have-a-highest-weight]] gives a primitive vector $v$ of $L(m)$, generating $L(m)$; [[prop-module-generated-by-a-primitive-vector]] gives that every weight is $m-2j$ with $j\ge0$ and, in its proof, that $L(m)$ is spanned by the orbit $U_{-\alpha}\cdot v$, while [[lem-normalizer-action-permutes-weight-spaces]] applies $w_0=-1$ to force the weights into $\{m,m-2,\dots,-m\}$. By [[lem-root-group-expansion-of-a-weight-vector]], $u_{-\alpha}(c)\cdot v=v+\sum_{i\ge1}c^iv_i$ with $v_i\in V_{m-2i}$; the nonzero $v_i$ lie in distinct weight spaces and span $L(m)$, so each weight space of $L(m)$ has dimension at most one and $\dim_kL(m)\le m+1$. The characteristic-$p$ computation verifies that $(g e_i)^p=g^{(p)}e_i^p$ in the symmetric power: for $g=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$ one has $g e_1^p=(ae_1+ce_2)^p=a^pe_1^p+c^pe_2^p$ and likewise for $e_2^p$, so $W=ke_1^p\oplus ke_2^p$ is a two-dimensional submodule. Its only $T$-stable lines are $ke_1^p$ and $ke_2^p$; neither is $G$-stable, because the negative root group sends $e_1^p$ to $e_1^p+c^pe_2^p$ and the reflection interchanges the two lines. Hence $W$ is simple with highest weight $p$, so $W\cong L(p)$ by the classification theorem.

items.title: Rational modules need not be semisimple in characteristic p
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers.
The claim that every finite-dimensional rational representation of a split
reductive group is semisimple is false. For every prime $p$ the following is a
counterexample
([[thm-complete-reducibility-of-rational-modules-in-characteristic-zero]]).
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p$ and let $G=\mathrm{SL}_2$ act on
$V=S^p(k^2)$, the symmetric power of the standard two-dimensional
representation, with $T_2$ acting through the characters $p,p-2,\dots,-p$
([[lem-sl2-structure-and-root-coordinates]],
[[ex-fundamental-sl2-modules-in-characteristic-p]]). Let $W\subseteq V$ be the
span of $e_1^p$ and $e_2^p$. Then $W$ is a two-dimensional simple submodule (the
Frobenius twist of $L(1)$), every simple submodule of $V$ equals $W$, so the
socle of $V$ is $W$, and $\dim_kV=p+1>2$. Hence $V$ is a nonsemisimple
finite-dimensional rational representation of the split reductive group
$\mathrm{SL}_2$, even though the dominant weights still classify the simple
rational representations
([[thm-dominant-weights-classify-simple-rational-modules-for-split-reductive-groups]]).
items.strategy: Direct proof on the current carrier: 1.1, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1; The basis monomials $e_1^ae_2^{p-a}$ of $V$ are $T_2$-eigenvectors of weights $(2a-p)\chi$ for $a=0,\dots,p$, i.e. of the characters $-p,-p+2,\dots,p$; each weight space of $V$ is therefore one-dimensional and spanned by a single monomial, and $T_2$ acts through the characters $p,p-2,\dots,-p$ as claimed.
